title: 500 Escudos (Nationalization of Mining)

obverse.description:
Red-brown on multicolor underprint.
Copper worker at left.
obverse.lettering:
BANCO CENTRAL 
DE CHILE
QUINIENTOS 
ESCUDOS
1971 AÑO DE LA NACIONALIZACIÓN DEL COBRE, SALITRE Y HIERRO
CASA DE MONEDA DE CHILE
obverse.lettering_translation:
Central Bank of Chile
Five Hundred Escudos
1971 - Year of the Nationalization of Cooper, Salitre and Iron
Chile Mint

reverse.description:
Dark-pink and gray.
Strip mining at center right (Open pit mine at Chuquicamata); 3-line text from Balmaceda at bottom.
reverse.lettering:
BANCO CENTRAL DE CHILE
QUINIENTOS ESCUDOS
"NO DEBEMOS CONSENTIR QUE ESTA VASTA
Y RICA REGION SEA CONVERTIDA EN UNA
SIMPLE FACTORIA EXTRANJERA" BALMACEDA.
reverse.lettering_translation:
Central Bank of Chile
Five Hundred Escudos
"We should not consent that this is vast and the rich region is becoming a simple foreign factory"

comments: Even though the Pesos was introduced in 1975, Banknotes of the Escudo were not officially withdrawn(by Decree Law N. 1123 Article 3; and Article 9) but formally, due to the rising inflation and the replacement of early banknotes with coins, these banknotes lost all of their worth by 1980. The Central Bank of Chile was not banned from printing or spending(until 31 December 1976, but only spendings authorized by the Ministry of Finance) the currency but they were required to be valued in the new currency unit or to be stamped with the new currency unit.
